title: Planet Opens Access to 10 Year Satellite Archive via New AI Tool
summary:
Planet has released a new search tool that uses artificial intelligence to help users analyze geospatial data using natural language. The company's Planet AI application is now open to the general public, granting users the ability to query a vast database of images captured by the company's satellite constellation.

The tool provides access to a daily satellite imagery archive containing more than 3,000 layers of data spanning a decade. During the application's beta phase, the company said the technology helped first responders track disaster paths and allowed park rangers to monitor illegal deforestation in real time.

selectedTweets.text:
Excited to announce that Planet AI is generally available! You can 'ask the Earth' 💬🌎 

Today's AI models have read the internet, but they haven't seen the world. The @planet AI app changes that. You can now ask questions directly to a 10+ year, 3,000+ layer archive of daily satellite imagery.

During beta, we've seen:
🌾 Farmers boosting crop yields
🚒 First responders tracking disaster paths
🛡️ Security teams uncovering emerging risks
🌲 Park rangers halting illegal deforestation in real time

We're putting satellite intelligence into more hands, helping more people see what's happening on Earth and make better decisions. Search. Analyse. Act.

What questions do you have? Try it now: https://t.co/4WV7PWdveG
